gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy each wheeled cooler uses per day, or how many hours a single battery runs it. On the same 288 Wh battery the compressor Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 ran for 51 hours in a reviewer's test (288 Wh ÷ 51 h = 5.6 W, about 136 Wh a day). Koolatron's own thermoelectric figure of 54 W with no thermostat works out to about 5.3 hours (288 Wh ÷ 54 W) and 1,296 Wh a day, roughly 9.5 times as much energy per day.
standout_why: I compared GearJunkie (rank 1), giftsitter (rank 2) and lovethe88 wheels (rank 5). Car and Driver (rank 8) blocked fetching, so I couldn't check it. GearJunkie gives only Anker's own claim ('299 Wh', 'up to 36 hours at 39 degrees') and a generic '40 to 70 W' range for 12V coolers that isn't tied to any model. It doesn't compare thermoelectric and compressor energy use per day. Giftsitter lists a 45/60 W rating for one BougeRV and no battery or runtime figures. Lovethe88 has no power, Wh or runtime figure for any model. None of them works out Wh per day or hours per battery for the Koolatron, VEVOR or Anker.
decides: This rules out the Koolatron 33 qt, which ChatGPT showed as a card at $226.79, for anyone running a cooler off a battery or power station rather than a running engine. It has no thermostat and draws about 54 W all the time, so a 288 Wh pack lasts about 5 hours, against about 51 hours for the compressor EverFrost 2 on the same pack. That supports a compressor model. Among the wheeled compressor models, the EverFrost 2 is the only one with a built-in battery whose runtime an independent reviewer measured. VEVOR's 0.2 kWh/24h claim is the maker's own and gives no test conditions.
